phone.text: Page 1 of 2; August 29, 2017 City Council Special Session Minutes MINUTES OF A SPECIAL SESSION OF THE VINEYARD CITY COUNCIL 240 East Gammon Road, Vineyard, Utah August 29, 2017 at 6:00 PM _______________ Present   Absent Mayor Randy Farnworth   Councilmember Tyce Flake Councilmember Julie Fullmer Councilmember Dale Goodman Councilmember Nate Riley Staff present:   City Manager/Finance Director Jacob McHargue, Public Works Director/City Engineer Don Overson, Deputy Chad Stilson with the Utah County Sheriff’s Department, City Planner Elizabeth Hart, City Recorder Pamela Spencer Others Present: Bronson Tatton with Flagship Homes 6:00 PM   SPECIAL SESSION Mayor Farnworth called the meeting to order at 6:00 PM. The invocation was given by Councilmember Goodman. CONSENT ITEMS a)   Approval of Willows at Waters Edge Final Plat C b)   Approval of Bridgeport at Water Edge Final Plat C c)   Approval of Westbrook at Waters Edge Final Plat C Mayor Farnworth called for comments. Councilmember Fullmer stated that she had no comments. Councilmember Riley expressed concerns over not knowing that the items would be on this agenda. Mayor Farnworth replied that it was something they felt they could get done. Mr. McHargue explained why they were on the agenda. Ms. Spencer mentioned that the reports were in the Dropbox on Monday. Councilmember Goodman stated that he thought that they were only doing the certification for the canvass of the election results. Council agreed to postpone the items to the next agenda. BUSINESS ITEMS 4.1   DISCUSSION AND ACTION – 2017 Municipal Primary Election Canvass and Certification The City Recorder Pamela Spencer will present to the Mayor and City Council the results of the 2017 Municipal Primary Election. The Mayor and City Council will sit as the Board of Canvassers to certify the results of the 2017 Primary Municipal Election. Mayor Farnworth turned the time over to City Recorder Pamela Spencer. Ms. Spencer went over the results of the 2017 Primary Election.

phone.text: Date Posted: October 22, 2019 VINEYARD PLANNING COMMISSION AND CITY COUNCIL   –   PUBLIC HEARING NOTICE Meeting Date: Planning Commission Public Hearing: November 6, 2019 at 6:00 PM City Council Public Hearing: November 13, 2019 at 6:00 PM Meeting Location: Vineyard City Hall, 125 South Main Street, Vineyard, UT 84059 (Both Hearings) Request:   The City of Vineyard is proposing zoning text amendments to the Vineyard Zoning Ordinance, including: Chapter 15.60 Home Day Care, Chapter 15.60 Home Preschool, 15.12.050 District Use Table, and Vineyard City Special Purpose Zoning Districts 5.08.010 to allow day cares and pre-schools to allow six (6) children in all zoning district as a permitted use, and up to 10 children in all zoning districts as a conditional use. Materials:   All documents, evidence and applicable code criteria are available for inspection at the Vineyard City Offices at no cost, or copies may be purchased for individual use. Written testimony submitted in advance of a public meeting is encouraged. During public hearings, the Planning Commission Chair or City Council reserves the right to limit the time allowed for oral testimony. Contact:   McKenna Marchant, Planning Tech, (801) 226-1929, or by email at mckennam@vineyardutah.org The start time for the public hearings listed above may begin later than posted due to agenda order and the nature of the discussion during the meeting. Any person having interest in this matter may attend and be heard during the public hearing. Written testimony may be submitted in writing at town hall or emailed to Elizabeth Hart at   elizabeth@vineyardutah.org . Written comments shall be submitted at least seven days in advance of the meeting in order to be entered into the record. One or more members of the Vineyard Planning Commission or City Council may participate electronically or   telephonically.   City   Codes   and   ordinances   are   available   on   the   City   website   found   at www.vineyard.utah.gov .Incompliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, individuals needing special accommodations during this meeting should notify Elizabeth Hart, Planner, with the City of Vineyard, at least 24 hours prior to the meeting by calling (801) 226-1929. I, the undersigned, hereby certify that the foregoing Public Hearing Notice will be published in the October 27 th   Sunday edition of the Salt Lake Tribune, posted at the Vineyard City Hall, Vineyard City Offices and the Vineyard City website, posted on the Utah Public Notice website, and delivered to surrounding affected entities. /s/ McKenna Marchant, Planning Tech

phone.text: NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING (ELECTRONIC MEETING) MAY 6, 2020 and MAY 13, 2020, 6:00 PM REQUEST:   To hear public comment in regards proposed to a Zoning Map and Text amendment. The applicant is proposing to rezone the property located at 720 S Geneva Road (Parcel Number 18:028:0179) consisting of 1.36 acres, from Business Park (BP) District to the Regional Commercial (RC) district. Additionally, an applicant is proposing to amend Chapter 15.38.030(2)(c) regarding parking requirements for offices and medical offices/clinics. The request is to change the stall requirement from one (1) stall per 200 square feet of floor area to one (1) stall per 250 square feet of floor area. CONTACT:   Elizabeth Hart, Senior Planner (801) 226-1929 or email at elizabeth@vineyardutah.org TIME & PLACE:   This meeting will be held electronically on for the Planning Commission on May 6, 2020 at 6:00 PM or as soon thereafter as possible, and for the City Council on May 13, 2020 at 6:00 PM or as soon thereafter as possible. Due to State mandates restricting mass gatherings, the public will not be allowed to attend in person. Public comments, questions, and requests for copies of application materials are encouraged to be emailed to Elizabeth Hart at   elizabeth@vineyardutah.org   prior to the meeting. All comments will be read into the record at the meeting. The hearing will be posted live for the public to view and to submit written comments during the meeting. The city will post instructions on the Vineyard City Website   www.vineyardutah.org allowing the public to participate live. In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act, individuals needing special accommodations during this meeting should notify Elizabeth Hart, at least 24 hours prior to the meeting by calling (801) 226-1929. I, the undersigned, hereby certify that the foregoing Public Notice was published in the April 26, 2020 edition of the Salt Lake Tribune and Deseret News, posted at the Vineyard City Offices, on the Vineyard website, and posted on the Utah Public Notice website. NOTICING COMPLETED ON:   April 23, 2020 CERTIFIED (NOTICED) BY: /s/ Morgan Brim Morgan Brim, Community Development Director

phone.text: MINUTES SPECIAL   MEETING DECEMBER   21,   1989 5:   30   p. m. The   Vineyard   Town   Council   held   a   special   meeting   on   Thursday in   the   basement   of   Grace   Holdaway'   s   home   to   discuss   the interlocal   agreement   with   Orem   City.   The   prayer   was   offered by   Rulon   Gammon. PRESENT   ABSENT J.   RULON   GAMMON,   MAYOR ROBERT   E.   HOLDAWAY,   COUNCILMAN MORRIS   G   CLEGG,   COUNCILMAN GRACE   HOLDAWAY,   COUNCILMEMBER STANLEY   W.   MORRIS,   COUNCILMAN CHERYL   HOLDAWAY,   CLERK DEAN   B.   ELLIS,   ATTORNEY INTERLOCAL   AGREEMENT The   Mayor   reported   of   meeting   with. Bryce   McEwan   from   IRMA to   discuss   the   contract   and   the   points   in   question   on   page 11.   Bryce   admitted   he   did   not   want   to   insure   us   based   on a   conflict   of   interest.   Rulon   also   spoke   with   Jim   Hill   from the   Fred   A.   Morton   Company,   a   private   provider,   who   carries Utah   County.   Mr. Hill   said   the   town   didn' t   have   enough   money to   pay   for   his   services   and   suggested   the   Utah   Local   Government Insurance   Trust.   Dean   suggested   a   separate   contract   with the   trust   to   cover   workers   compensation.   Since   we   don'   t have   a   compensation   fund   for   Orem   employees   we   cannot   get insurance   to   cover   us.   Dean   suggested   the   standard   way   would be   for   Vineyard   to   pay   Orem'   s   liability   and   then   Orem   would cover   us.   The   Mayor   felt   everything   in   the   contract   is   in order   except   the   personnel   and   workmans   comp.   Since   Orem'   s council   does   not   meet   again   until   January   Stan   suggested we   go   ahead   and   sign   the   contract.   The   contract   states   it can   be   cancelled   with   a   thirty   day   notice.   Council   agreed to   sign   the   contract   to   provide   services   effective   January 1,   1990. Stuart   Taylor   from   Orem   made   a   committment   we   would   be   on the   agenda   January   9th.   Stan   suggested   we   attend   the   meeting and   extend   a   dollar   figure   that   would   be   appropriate.   Dean spoke   with   Nathan   Clark   from   the   trust   who   stated   we   could possibly   buy   a   policy   on   Orem   that   would   cover   Vineyard. The   policy   would   need   to   have   the   specific   names   of   the individuals   from   Orem   who   need   to   be   covered.   We   will   receive the   dollar   figure   on   that   type   of   policy   from   the   trust. Robert   Holdaway   made   the   motion   to   ratify   the   contract   to seek   coverage   for   the   remaining   liability.   Morris   Clegg seconded.   Passed   unanimously.

phone.text: Page 1 of 8; September 27, 2017 Vineyard Redevelopment Agency Minutes MINUTES OF A MEETING OF THE VINEYARD REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY BOARD 240 East Gammon Road, Vineyard, Utah September 27, 2017 – 6:00 PM Present   Absent Chair Randy Farnworth Boardmember Tyce Flake Boardmember Julie Fullmer Boardmember Dale Goodman Boardmember Nate Riley Staff Present:   City Manager/Finance Director Jacob McHargue, Public Works Director/Engineer Don Overson, Economic Development Director Morgan Brim, Building Official George Reid, Sergeant Holden Rockwell with the Utah County Sheriff’s Department, Water/Sewer Operator Sullivan Love, Records Management Assistant Kelly Kloepfer Others Present:   Residents Shawn Herring, Teresa Goodman, David Lauret, and Kyle Stucki; Jeff Gochnour with Cottonwood Partners 7:16 PM   RDA Meeting Chair Farnworth opened the RDA meeting at 7:16 PM. CONSENT AGENDA: No items were submitted. ITEMS REQUESTED FOR FUTURE AGENDAS No items were submitted. BUSINESS ITEMS: 3.1   DISCUSSION AND ACTION   –   State Infrastructure Bank Loan City Manager/Finance Director Jacob McHargue will present an update for the State Infrastructure Bank Loan. The Board will take appropriate action. Mr. McHargue explained the history of the loan, authorized by the Transportation Commission in 2013. He pointed out that the money was initially approved to remove the rail spur, and was not approved for any other project. On September 15, 2017 Mr. McHargue and Chair Farnworth met with the Transportation Commission, which approved some loan modifications. These modifications allowed for flexibility, which would allow the board to spend the money on the following projects: -   Center Street overpass -   FrontRunner Station -   UP Rail spur -   Vineyard Connector extension
